13:1.sourceText: Ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ἐκείνῃ ἐξελθὼν ὁ Ἰησοῦς τῆς οἰκίας ἐκάθητο παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν·
13:1.targetText: And in that day Jesus, having gone forth from the house, was sitting by the sea,

groups.note: The actual genitive article/house phrase supplies the departure source, rendered from the house without a separately written Greek from preposition.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with that day or Jesus.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an opening And; pinned N1904 begins with in that day without a separately written coordinator.

13:2.sourceText: καὶ συνήχθησαν πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλοι πολλοί, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ἐπὶ τὸν αἰγιαλὸν εἱστήκει.
13:2.targetText: and gathered together to Him were many multitudes, so that He having gone into the boat sat down, and all the multitude on the beach stood,

groups.note: The actual accusative pronoun is the subject of the result infinitive, expressed as He in LSV’s recast finite result clause. The same personal identity remains without a different nominative Greek pronoun.
The actual sitting infinitive is rendered finite sat down in the result clause, retaining the same sitting event with that construction change explicit.

13:3.sourceText: καὶ ἐλάλησεν αὐτοῖς πολλὰ ἐν παραβολαῖς λέγων Ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων τοῦ σπείρειν.
13:3.targetText: and He spoke to them many things in allegories, saying, “Behold, the sower went forth to sow,

groups.note: The actual comparison/parable noun παραβολή is rendered allegories by LSV. The original head remains παραβολή, not an invented ἀλληγορία noun or a conclusion about how every story detail must be interpreted.
The actual article and sowing participle designate the sowing person, rendered the sower without a separately written Greek sower noun.
The actual genitive article with the sowing infinitive expresses the purpose to sow; both source constituents retain this complete infinitive construction.

13:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐν τῷ σπείρειν αὐτὸν ἃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἐλθόντα τὰ πετεινὰ κατέφαγεν αὐτά.
13:4.targetText: and in his sowing, some indeed fell by the way, and the birds having come, devoured them,

groups.note: The actual articular sowing infinitive is rendered nominally sowing, while its separately identified personal subject is English his. The source article and infinitive remain one nominal action constituent.
The actual neuter-plural relative ἃ introduces the seed portion, rendered partitive some; it is not relabeled as an independently written Greek indefinite-pronoun lemma.

13:5.sourceText: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθέως ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς,
13:5.targetText: and others fell on the rocky places where they did not have much earth, and immediately they sprang forth, through having no depth of earth,

groups.note: The actual substantival rocky adjective denotes rocky ground/places, rendered rocky places without a separate Greek place noun.

Greek has singular finite agreement with the neuter-plural seed subject; English naturally uses plural they sprang forth. The original singular form is retained rather than presented as a different textual reading.
The actual article and having infinitive form the nominal action after through, rendered having; the separately anchored negative retains no with its depth object.

13:6.sourceText: ἡλίου δὲ ἀνατείλαντος ἐκαυματίσθη καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
13:6.targetText: and the sun having risen they were scorched, and through having no root, they withered,

groups.note: The actual genitive sun is the subject of the risen genitive-absolute circumstance; English the sun names that same participant without changing the displayed original case.
The actual singular Greek verb agrees with the neuter-plural seed subject; LSV uses plural they were scorched for those same seeds.

13:7.sourceText: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ ἀπέπνιξαν αὐτά.
13:7.targetText: and others fell on the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked them,

13:8.sourceText: ἄλλα δὲ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν καὶ ἐδίδου καρπόν, ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.
13:8.targetText: and others fell on the good ground, and were giving fruit, some indeed a hundredfold, and some sixty, and some thirty.

groups.note: The actual singular giving verb agrees with the neuter-plural seed subject; LSV uses plural were giving for the same fruitful seeds.
The actual hundred numeral specifies the yield rate, rendered a hundredfold. English fold expresses that numerical yield construction without a separately written Greek fold/times word.

unmappedSource.reason: The repeated attributive Greek article at good is not separately expressed in the one English good-ground designation.

13:9.targetText: He who is having ears to hear—let him hear.”

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV follows the longer ears-to-hear reading; pinned N1904 writes ears directly followed by the hearing imperative, without a separate infinitive to hear.

13:10.sourceText: Καὶ προσελθόντες οἱ μαθηταὶ εἶπαν αὐτῷ Διὰ τί ἐν παραβολαῖς λαλεῖς αὐτοῖς;
13:10.targetText: And the disciples having come near, said to Him, “Why do You speak to them in allegories?”

13:11.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν ὅτι Ὑμῖν δέδοται γνῶναι τὰ μυστήρια τῆς βασιλείας τῶν οὐρανῶν, ἐκείνοις δὲ οὐ δέδοται.
13:11.targetText: And He answering said to them that, “To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of the heavens, and to these it has not been given,

groups.note: The actual dative demonstrative ἐκείνοις designates those recipients; LSV refers to that same contrasted group as to these. The actual source demonstrative and its grammatical form are retained, not relabeled as a different Greek near-demonstrative lemma.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly states the saying recipients to them; pinned N1904 writes said that before the separate To-you gift-recipient phrase, without a personal saying recipient here.

13:12.sourceText: ὅστις γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ καὶ περισσευθήσεται· ὅστις δὲ οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
13:12.targetText: for whoever has, it will be given to him, and he will have overabundance, and whoever has not, even that which he has will be taken from him.

groups.note: The actual passive abundance verb περισσευθήσεται is rendered he will have overabundance. The full English abundance-state expression retains that one real predicate without a separately invented Greek have verb.

13:13.sourceText: διὰ τοῦτο ἐν παραβολαῖς αὐτοῖς λαλῶ, ὅτι βλέποντες οὐ βλέπουσιν καὶ ἀκούοντες οὐκ ἀκούουσιν οὐδὲ συνίουσιν.
13:13.targetText: Because of this, in allegories I speak to them, because seeing they do not see, and hearing they do not hear, nor understand,

13:14.sourceText: καὶ ἀναπληροῦται αὐτοῖς ἡ προφητεία Ἡσαΐου ἡ λέγουσα Ἀκοῇ ἀκούσετε καὶ οὐ μὴ συνῆτε, καὶ βλέποντες βλέψετε καὶ οὐ μὴ ἴδητε.
13:14.targetText: and fulfilled on them is the prophecy of Isaiah that says, With hearing you will hear, and you will not understand, and seeing you will see, and you will not perceive,

groups.note: The actual present saying participle is rendered finite says in the prophecy description; the actual speaking head remains distinct from its preceding article that.
The actual dative hearing noun expresses the hearing-with-hearing idiom, rendered With hearing without a separately written Greek with preposition.
The actual οὐ μή pair gives the one English not in the emphatic negative prediction; the understanding verb retains the prospective English you will understand wording.
The second actual οὐ μή pair gives the second English not, preserving both original negatives within one emphatic construction.

13:15.sourceText: ἐπαχύνθη γὰρ ἡ καρδία τοῦ λαοῦ τούτου, καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν βαρέως ἤκουσαν, καὶ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτῶν ἐκάμμυσαν· μή ποτε ἴδωσιν τοῖς ὀφθαλμοῖς καὶ τοῖς ὠσὶν ἀκούσωσιν καὶ τῇ καρδίᾳ συνῶσιν καὶ ἐπιστρέψωσιν, καὶ ἰάσομαι αὐτούς.
13:15.targetText: for the heart of this people was made obtuse, and with the ears they barely heard, and they closed their eyes, lest they might see with the eyes, and might hear with the ears, and understand with the heart, and turn back, and I might heal them.

groups.note: The actual dative article/ears phrase gives the means of hearing, expressed as with the ears; its complete case-governed relation is retained without a Greek with preposition.

The actual heavily/with-difficulty adverb βαρέως is rendered barely in the hearing description; this retains the difficult-hearing sense rather than inventing a different Greek quantity adverb. Primary dictionary: https://www.billmounce.com/greek-dictionary/bareos.
The actual dative eyes phrase gives the means of seeing, rendered with the eyes as a complete case-governed expression.
The second actual dative ears phrase belongs to the might-hear clause and retains the second English with-the-ears occurrence.
The actual dative heart phrase gives the means/sphere of understanding, rendered with the heart without an independently written Greek with preposition.

N1904 has future indicative I will heal, ἰάσομαι; LSV uses I might heal within its lest construction. The healing head remains while the source future and English modal wording are explicitly distinguished.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with their eyes.

13:16.sourceText: ὑμῶν δὲ μακάριοι οἱ ὀφθαλμοὶ ὅτι βλέπουσιν, καὶ τὰ ὦτα ὑμῶν ὅτι ἀκούουσιν.
13:16.targetText: And blessed are your eyes because they see, and your ears because they hear,

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek articles are not separately expressed with your eyes or your ears.

unmappedTarget.reason: English supplies a copula in the blessed-your-eyes nominal expression; no Greek be verb is written here.

13:17.sourceText: ἀμὴν γὰρ λέγω ὑμῖν ὅτι πολλοὶ προφῆται καὶ δίκαιοι ἐπεθύμησαν ἰδεῖν ἃ βλέπετε καὶ οὐκ εἶδαν, καὶ ἀκοῦσαι ἃ ἀκούετε καὶ οὐκ ἤκουσαν.

13:18.sourceText: Ὑμεῖς οὖν ἀκούσατε τὴν παραβολὴν τοῦ σπείραντος.

13:21.targetText: and he has no root in himself, but is temporary, and persecution or tribulation having happened because of the word, immediately he is stumbled.

groups.note: The actual happening genitive-absolute circumstance qualifies the tribulation/persecution event; English reverses the order of the two nouns but retains their actual original identities.

13:22.sourceText: ὁ δὲ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων, καὶ ἡ μέριμνα τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου συμπνίγει τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.

13:23.sourceText: ὁ δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν καλὴν γῆν σπαρείς, οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ τὸν λόγον ἀκούων καὶ συνιείς, ὃς δὴ καρποφορεῖ καὶ ποιεῖ ὃ μὲν ἑκατὸν ὃ δὲ ἑξήκοντα ὃ δὲ τριάκοντα.

13:24.sourceText: Ἄλλην παραβολὴν παρέθηκεν αὐτοῖς λέγων Ὡμοιώθη ἡ βασιλεία τῶν οὐρανῶν ἀνθρώπῳ σπείραντι καλὸν σπέρμα ἐν τῷ ἀγρῷ αὐτοῦ.

unmappedSource.reason: The Greek article is not separately expressed with his field.

13:25.sourceText: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους ἦλθεν αὐτοῦ ὁ ἐχθρὸς καὶ ἐπέσπειρεν ζιζάνια ἀνὰ μέσον τοῦ σίτου καὶ ἀπῆλθεν.

13:26.sourceText: ὅτε δὲ ἐβλάστησεν ὁ χόρτος καὶ καρπὸν ἐποίησεν, τότε ἐφάνη καὶ τὰ ζιζάνια.

The actual making verb with fruit is the fruit-producing construction, rendered yielded ... fruit. The source making head is not silently replaced with a different Greek bearing verb.

13:27.sourceText: προσελθόντες δὲ οἱ δοῦλοι τοῦ οἰκοδεσπότου εἶπον αὐτῷ Κύριε, οὐχὶ καλὸν σπέρμα ἔσπειρας ἐν τῷ σῷ ἀγρῷ; πόθεν οὖν ἔχει ζιζάνια;
